title: The Lunch Tin with Two Initials
title_ja: 二つの頭文字が刻まれた弁当箱

source_links.title: Original fictional lesson — project authoring provenance, not factual evidence

fact_notes: 完全オリジナルの架空事例。実在の学校・人物・調査結果を示さない。リンクは制作方針の来歴確認用。

sentences.en: During a visit to a local museum, Rina saw an old metal lunch tin in a glass case.
sentences.ja: 地元の博物館を訪れた際、リナはガラスケースに入った古い金属製の弁当箱を見ました。

sentences.en: It had two different sets of initials on its lid, which made her curious.
sentences.ja: ふたには異なる二組の頭文字があり、彼女は興味を持ちました。

sentences.en: At first, she thought the tin had belonged to two people at the same time.
sentences.ja: 最初、二人が同時にその弁当箱を所有していたと考えました。

sentences.en: However, a museum worker showed her a written record that came with the object.
sentences.ja: しかし博物館の職員はその品物と一緒に届いた記録を見せました。

sentences.en: According to the record, the first owner had given the tin to his younger brother many years later.
sentences.ja: 記録によると、最初の持ち主は何年も後に弟に弁当箱を譲っていました。

sentences.en: The brother added his own initials without removing the earlier ones.
sentences.ja: 弟は以前の頭文字を消さずに自分の頭文字を追加しました。

sentences.en: Rina realized that the marks could tell a story about an object passing from one person to another.
sentences.ja: リナはその印が、品物が人から人へ渡った物語を語り得ると気づきました。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the worker explained that the marks alone did not prove the story.
sentences.ja: それでも職員は印だけではその話を証明できないと説明しました。

sentences.en: The written record was useful because it gave information that the object itself could not provide.
sentences.ja: 記録は品物そのものでは示せない情報を与えるため役立ちました。

sentences.en: After returning to school, Rina began to ask her family about objects they had kept for a long time.
sentences.ja: 学校に戻ってから、リナは長く保管されてきた品物について家族に尋ね始めました。

sentences.en: She discovered that even ordinary things might have a history worth recording.
sentences.ja: ありふれた物でも記録する価値のある歴史があるかもしれないと発見しました。

sentences.en: This time, she tried to separate what she could see from what people told her.
sentences.ja: 今度は、自分で見えることと人から聞いたことを分けようとしました。

vocabulary.definition: a usually hard material such as iron
a container used to protect things
the top that closes a container

questions.prompt: Where did Rina see the tin?
Who received the tin from its first owner?
What did the brother do with the earlier initials?
options: He copied them onto a wall
questions.explanation_ja: 以前の頭文字は消さなかった。

questions.prompt: Why did Rina's first idea change?
options: The tin was not made of metal
The record described a later transfer
She learned the museum was closed
questions.explanation_ja: 同時所有ではなく後年に譲った記録。

questions.prompt: What could the marks alone not prove?
options: The story of how the tin changed owners
The presence of two sets of initials
That the object was in a case
questions.explanation_ja: 所有の経緯は印だけでは証明できない。

questions.prompt: Why was the written record useful?
options: It gave the tin a new owner
It supplied information not visible on the tin
questions.explanation_ja: 物そのものでは分からない情報。

questions.prompt: What did Rina do after returning to school?
questions.explanation_ja: 家族の品物について尋ねた。

options: Objects and records can offer different historical evidence
Initials always reveal the full history of an object
Only valuable objects have a history
Museum workers should avoid written records
questions.explanation_ja: 物と記録を区別しながら歴史を考える。

grammar.explanation_ja: 過去完了で考えた時点より前。

paraphrases.source: It had two different sets of initials on its lid, which made her curious.
paraphrases.rewrite: The two pairs of letters on the cover attracted her interest.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: ふたの二組の文字に興味を持った。

paraphrases.source: According to the record, the first owner had given the tin to his younger brother many years later.
paraphrases.rewrite: The record said the original owner later passed it on to his brother.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 記録によれば後で弟に譲った。

paraphrases.source: Nevertheless, the worker explained that the marks alone did not prove the story.
paraphrases.rewrite: The worker said the marks were not enough evidence by themselves.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 印だけでは証拠が足りない。

paraphrases.source: This time, she tried to separate what she could see from what people told her.
paraphrases.rewrite: She distinguished her own observations from other people's accounts.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 観察と他者の話を区別。

discourse.role_ja: 初期の推測と記録の対照。
記録という情報源を明示。
印の意味と証明できない限界。

cloze.explanation_ja: 話の真実性を証明する。
観察と伝聞を区別する。
